# AI rules — MCP servers (Node.js + TypeScript)

Scope: `mcp-servers/**` — a separate product that lives in this repository for now and must stay
movable to its own repository as it is. See
[ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md) §3 and the design documents in
[mcp-servers/docs/design/](mcp-servers/docs/design/).

These rules describe **only** `mcp-servers/`. The web app keeps its own rules
([AI.md](AI.md), [AI_FRONTEND.md](AI_FRONTEND.md), [AI_PROXY.md](AI_PROXY.md),
[AI_WEB_DESIGN_SQOWE.md](AI_WEB_DESIGN_SQOWE.md)); the sentence in
[CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md) that the project has "no database, backend framework, React, TypeScript or
Docker" describes the web app alone.

## Language and runtime

- **TypeScript**, run directly by Node (type stripping). **No build step, no bundler, no
  transpiler, no `tsc` emit.** `tsc --noEmit` is the type check.
- Node **24 or newer**. `node:sqlite`, `node:test` and `fetch` are used as they are.
- Only syntax Node can erase: **no `enum`, no `namespace`, no constructor parameter properties,
  no `import =`**. `tsconfig.json` sets `erasableSyntaxOnly`, so `npm run typecheck` catches it.
- Imports carry the file extension: `import { x } from './m3u.ts'`. `allowImportingTsExtensions` is
  on and `noEmit` is set, so this is what TypeScript expects.
- `verbatimModuleSyntax` is on: type-only imports must use `import type`.
- `strict`, `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` and `noImplicitOverride` are on. Array access returns
  `T | undefined` — handle it.

## Layout

```
mcp-servers/
  src/shared/     code used by both servers
  src/cinema/     the Cinema server
  src/tv-guide/   the TV Guide server
  tests/          node:test suites
  scripts/        local scripts, not part of the server
  docs/design/    the design documents
```

- Keep each file **~600 lines or less**. Split a module before it grows past that.
- One module, one job. `shared/` holds nothing that only one server uses.
- **Nothing outside `mcp-servers/` may import from it, and it imports nothing from outside it**
  except its own npm dependencies. Ported web app logic is copied, not imported, and the copy
  names the source file and function in a comment.

## Modules and libraries

- Exact dependency versions in `package.json`; `package-lock.json` is committed.
- The dependencies are few and deliberate: `@modelcontextprotocol/server`, `zod`, `sqlite-vec`,
  `snowball-stemmers`. A new dependency needs a reason in the pull request.
- `snowball-stemmers` is the exact file the web app ships in `public/vendor/` (same sha256), so
  the stemming behaviour is identical. `src/types/snowball-stemmers.d.ts` holds its types.

## The working folder

- Every server takes `--data-dir`. It holds `settings.json`, `raw/`, the databases, `refresh.lock`
  and `logs/`.
- `settings.json` is the only file the owner edits. The server reads it, validates it, and writes
  **only** the template (mode `0600`) when it does not exist. It never rewrites the file.
- Settings are re-read when the file changes on disk, so an edited URL takes effect without a
  restart.
- The URLs come from the settings file only. Never from the environment.

## Secrets

- The provider URL carries the account's access key. **A full provider URL never appears in a log
  line, in `get_status`, or in a list result.** Use `maskUrl` from `shared/links.ts`.
- `settings.json` is created with mode `0600`; the databases and the log file too. The mode is a
  **post-condition**: it is set after every write, not only when a file is created, because the
  mode of `createWriteStream` only counts for a new file.
- The working folder and the folders this server creates are `0700`. **A folder that existed
  before — `/tmp`, `/var`, the home folder — is never touched**: `ensureDir` only makes private
  the folders it created and the working folder itself.
- The OpenRouter key is read from the environment and never logged.
- Play links appear only in the detail tools.

## Downloads

- Only `http:` and `https:` are fetched. The scheme is checked before the request.
- The redirects are followed by hand (`redirect: 'manual'`): a redirect from `https` to `http` is
  refused **before** the target is requested, and the number of hops is capped.
- The download goes to `<name>.part` and only replaces the previous copy when it is complete. An
  empty file, a file that cannot be made private, and a file that fails the content check leave the
  last good copy in place. The check runs **before** the swap, never after it.

## stdout

- **stdout carries the MCP protocol and nothing else.** Logs go to
  `<data-dir>/logs/server.log`; a fallback goes to stderr. `console.log` is not allowed in the
  server code — use the logger.

## URLs

- Every URL that leaves the server goes through `sanitizeUrl` (`shared/links.ts`), a port of the
  web app's helper. Only `http:` and `https:` are allowed. **The check is never relaxed** to make
  data pass; a rejected URL is dropped and counted.

## Time

- Every absolute time comes from the raw source string **with its offset**
  (`parseProviderTimestamp` in `shared/time.ts`). No offset-less parsing, anywhere.
- Times are stored as integer UTC epoch seconds; the raw string is kept next to them.

## Storage

- SQLite through the built-in `node:sqlite`, with the `sqlite-vec` extension loaded
  (`allowExtension: true`). WAL mode, foreign keys on.
- The vectors live in their own file (`vectors.sqlite`), so that deleting the catalogue database
  does not throw away paid-for vectors.
- Migrations are idempotent. A refresh writes into staging tables and swaps them in, so readers
  never see a half-written catalogue.

## Search

- FTS5 has no Russian stemmer: the text is stemmed (Snowball, by detected language) **before** it
  goes into the index, and the query is stemmed the same way.
- Vectors of different models are never compared.
- Search works when the embeddings are disabled, when the key is missing, and while the vectors
  are still being built.

## Tests

- `node:test`, run with `npm test` (`node --test 'tests/**/*.test.ts'`). Every phase ends with
  `npm run typecheck` and `npm test` green.
- Fixtures live in `tests/fixtures/` and are hand-made: hosts are `example.invalid`, keys are
  `KEY`. **Never copy `tmp/` files or a real URL into the repository.**
- OpenRouter is faked in the tests. A live run only happens with `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` and
  `IPTV_MCP_LIVE=1` set.
- A change to a shared module changes both servers: the test belongs next to the module.
